## 開篇固定收益主論點

8月27日美國固定收益市場收盤，美債延續賣壓，但幅度僅為最小變動單位；價格結構仍把舉證責任留給押注政策轉向寬鬆的投資人。2年期殖利率上升1個基點至4.20%，10年期上升1個基點至4.67%，30年期亦上升1個基點至5.19%。各年期平行上移，使2s10s維持47個基點、2s30s維持99個基點。10年期實質殖利率持平於2.34%，損益兩平通膨率上升1個基點至2.33%，顯示當日邊際壓力來自通膨補償，而非實質折現率再度上升。美債供給並非阻力：財政部標售$440億7年期公債，需求穩健，殖利率仍收高。最新數據與Fed官員發言使政策反應函數更難判定，市場因此在Fed主席Kevin Warsh首次於傑克森霍爾發表演說前計入小幅溢價。

美國最新證據方向不一，但通膨敏感訊號更能主導收盤走勢。截至8月22日當週，初領失業救濟金人數由修正後的20.7萬降至20.3萬，低於市場共識的20.8萬；續領失業救濟金人數為177.8萬。勞動市場並未出現足以迫使Fed忽略高於目標通膨的轉折。7月商品貿易逆差初值由$1,014億大幅擴至$1,188億，市場共識為$990億。逆差擴大使成長判讀更複雜，但也反映外部融資需求加重，不能直接視為通膨降溫訊號。在此背景下，堪薩斯市Fed總裁Jeff Schmid與克里夫蘭Fed總裁Beth Hammack均主張，目前政策對經濟的抑制仍不足；波士頓Fed總裁Susan Collins持續認為政策略具限制性，芝加哥Fed總裁Austan Goolsbee則希望看到更多服務通膨證據。收盤價格反映的是政策究竟有無限制性的實質辯論，而不只是限制性政策應維持多久。

風險偏好明顯限制了利率市場的看空解讀。Nvidia財測帶動那斯達克100指數上漲1.43%，半導體指數上漲2.33%；即使S&P 500多數成分股下跌，指數仍上漲0.72%，VIX則下跌4.60%至14.51。廣泛信用債總報酬基金近乎持平，並未顯示融資活動失序撤退。荷莫茲海峽周邊外交斡旋再遇阻力，WTI上漲1.57%至$83.52，Brent上漲0.82%至$88.56，逆轉前一交易日部分能源價格緩解。不過，通過海峽的實體流量已回升至每日約600萬至800萬桶，仍僅為戰前水準的一半左右。科技股、油價與損益兩平通膨率同步走強，較符合名目需求具韌性、供給壓力尚未消退的情境，而非全面性的財政恐慌。

因此，投資委員會的判斷範圍雖窄，影響卻相當關鍵。美債殖利率僅上升1個基點，但初領失業救濟金數據穩健、貿易逆差擴大、油價反彈，加上Fed內部鷹派聲量轉強，都使前一交易日勉強成立的暫緩判斷難以令人安心。強勁AI需求另添一項挑戰：一方面支撐股市成長預期，另一方面也加劇勞動力、設備、電力與債券市場承接能力的競爭。全球央行實際升息及轉趨強硬的指引，進一步強化這股壓力。市場對美債將持續遭到拋售的信心仍有限，因殖利率曲線並未變陡、10年期實質殖利率未上升、7年期標售需求穩健，且實體原油出口持續復甦。Warsh如今必須決定，是以更清晰的緊縮框架確認市場計入的小幅通膨溢價，還是說明Fed將如何區分集中於AI的強勁需求、供給衝擊與整體經濟過熱，藉此抑制長端利率波動。

## Fed辯論轉向政策是否具有限制性

Schmid提出當日最明確的新增政策訊號。這位堪薩斯市Fed總裁表示，目前利率設定在短端可能仍具寬鬆性，立場接近7月支持升息的官員。聯邦基金利率目標區間目前為3.5%至3.75%，Fed偏好的通膨指標截至7月的一年升幅為3.7%；Schmid認為，決策官員仍須有所作為，才能稱政策具有限制性。這不只是保留再次升息的選項，而是質疑委員會評估通膨持續性時採用的政策起點。

Hammack則把這項看法推得更遠，並明確主張行動時點。這位克里夫蘭Fed總裁是7月主張升息25個基點的3名異議官員之一；她表示，目前利率不足以使經濟降溫，官員應立即行動。她預期2026年底通膨約為3%，明年向2%中段回落的進展也相當有限。她擔心的並非通膨預期已經失控；她明確表示尚未發生。真正風險在於，通膨高於目標超過5年，最終可能改變家庭行為。Hammack也指出，股權與債務資本市場異常活躍，證明金融環境未產生足夠的限制作用。她把政策反應函數連結至實際的風險承擔與發債活動，而非只看落後的通膨數據。

Collins描述的是較傳統的傳導機制。這位今年無投票權、且支持7月按兵不動的波士頓Fed總裁，仍認為房市與小型企業正受到溫和限制。她是否繼續支持利率不變，取決於通膨降溫的證據，尤其在關稅、中東局勢或其他供給衝擊可能延長通膨壓力之際。她也判斷，通膨預期仍與2%目標一致。這些條件使鷹派論點無法成為共識：部分經濟活動正對高借貸成本作出反應，衡量政策可信度的指標也尚未迫使官員立即行動。

Goolsbee設定的門檻進一步釐清歧見來源。這位芝加哥Fed總裁準備等待證據，以判斷目前的通膨衝擊是否持續，其中服務價格最為關鍵。若服務通膨持續偏高或惡化，他的疑慮將升高；若服務通膨降溫，則仍有耐心觀望的空間。因此，委員會的分歧涵蓋3個不應簡化為單一鷹鴿光譜的問題：目前政策是否具有限制性、供給推動的通膨是否會擴散，以及採取行動前需要多少證據。Schmid與Hammack對第一個問題的答案是否定的；Collins認為限制作用已經出現；Goolsbee則將下一步決策繫於服務通膨的廣度與持續性。

週四公布的數據未能化解歧見。初領失業救濟金人數為20.3萬，較共識低5,000人，也較修正後前值低4,000人，支持勞動市場仍足以承受更緊政策的看法。商品貿易逆差擴大$174億，幅度遠超預期，但單憑這項數據無法辨識內需或庫存的貢獻。對固定收益市場而言，數據的即時意義在於成長核算不確定性與外部失衡擴大同時出現。兩項數據都未顯示廣泛需求惡化，因此無法證明4.20%的2年期殖利率顯然過高。

短端利率交易仍不認同即將升息。市場出現一筆4.5萬口10月聯邦基金期貨的大額買盤，反映12月前利率不變；與此同時，整體市場仍給予9月升息約三分之一的機率，並計入年底前升息25個基點。官員強硬發言與特定會議日期定價之間的落差，解釋了附息債殖利率曲線為何平行移動，而非前端大幅重定價。投資人為Warsh相關風險支付小幅溢價，但未將Schmid與Hammack視為已取得委員會多數支持。

長端同樣承受溝通溢價。即使明確的通膨反應函數偏向鷹派，只要政策路徑更清晰，仍可降低不確定性；若缺乏說明，每一次供給衝擊、數據發布與美債操作都會左右邊際政策敘事。2s30s斜率不變，顯示週四並未演變成新一波債務可持續性疑慮所驅動的曲線陡峭化。不過，30年期殖利率為5.19%、2年期為4.20%，兩者仍相差接近1個百分點，因此貨幣政策與債務管理政策如何互動的不確定性，代價依然高昂。Warsh的任務不只是展現限制性立場，而是說明哪些證據足以推動Fed改變政策，以及哪些資產負債表問題仍不屬於利率決策範圍。

## AI成長同步推升需求與融資成本

Nvidia將AI需求敘事從預估資本支出，轉化為已實現的企業成長訊號。公司預測2028會計年度營收將成長約70%，高於分析師原先預期的45%，並預估本期營收為$1,080億，較一年前成長89%。股價上漲近9%，市值增加約$4,420億，並帶動科技股指數走高。較小型客戶貢獻約$400億，占單季營收42%，占比較一年前增加逾一倍。客戶基礎擴大，削弱需求僅仰賴少數超大規模雲端業者的論點，即使記憶體、晶圓與封裝供給限制仍是交付能力的關鍵。

對固定收益市場而言，相同財測也強化Schmid所指出的名目需求傳導。資料中心建設會競逐勞動力、機械、材料與電力。即使住宅建設疲弱，商品生產與營建業的薪資增幅仍快於服務業；Schmid也表示，AI投資正加劇其轄區內的競爭。總體經濟的關鍵是，這些壓力能否維持足夠集中，使Fed得以容忍，或會廣泛擴散，進而延續服務與薪資通膨。週四10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1個基點、實質殖利率持平，方向上符合市場小幅重估這條通膨傳導管道。單一基點無法確立因果，但價格結構較符合名目需求具韌性，而非成長恐慌。

Nvidia揭露的承諾顯示，在傳統債務出現前，股市樂觀情緒如何產生債權人曝險。公司已承諾未來支出$2,790億，多數涉及Samsung Electronics、SK Hynix、Micron Technology與Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing。即使產能未被使用，公司也承諾支付最高$560億的資料中心使用費，並承擔$1,090億貸款保證，多數與OpenAI在俄亥俄州的一座大型資料中心有關。採購承諾、使用保證與信用保證的法律地位各不相同，但當使用率、客戶品質或再融資條件不如預期時，都可能競逐現金。已實現的銷售前景改善了這項計算中的收入面，卻不會使或有義務消失。

債券投資人已要求產業為市場承接支付代價。超大規模雲端業者今年已透過7種貨幣籌資逾$2,200億；JPMorgan歐洲投資級融資主管Matthias Reschke估計，其美國債券相較其他公司債的利差溢價約為55個基點。他的結論是，只要價格到位，市場仍有承接能力。因此，這項溢價並非市場關閉的訊號，而是在規模較小的貨幣市場中，異常龐大的發債集中於可能迅速成為主要非金融發行人的借款人時，所需支付的出清成本。

Volta Infrastructure為下一階段建設提供一筆界定明確的交易。JPMorgan已開始向貸款機構探詢一筆$50億債務融資案，以支應這家新公司的資料中心。Volta先前以$24億估值取得$3億創投資金，並簽署一份為期6年、價值$100億的協議，在一座由Bitdeer Technologies共同管理的挪威據點向Anthropic提供運算能力。這筆融資仰賴合約客戶關係、據點交付與基礎設施執行，而非成熟超大規模雲端業者的無擔保信用。最終槓桿、擔保品、攤還安排、保證與貸款人保障，將決定該合約是否足以支撐所要求的債務。

其他借款人也正因應相同的資本競爭而調整融資市場。Fortescue考慮首次發行熊貓債，規模約人民幣30億元，將由Fortescue Treasury (China)發行、母公司提供保證；投資人會議預計於9月初舉行，最快可能於10月展開銷售。公司已申請在2年內發行最多人民幣200億元。今年熊貓債平均票息為1.88%，比3年期美債殖利率低逾200個基點；即使Fortescue與中國國營鐵礦砂買家之間的爭議干擾部分出口，熊貓債仍提供一條低成本的融資分散管道。融資管道與商業摩擦存在於同一架構中：母公司保證支持當地投資人，而發行人與中國的關係，也正是公司必須分散融資市場與銷售來源的部分原因。

Moderna利用的則是另一種資產價格窗口。正面的癌症疫苗試驗結果帶動公司股價在8月19日單日上漲177%後，Moderna宣布發行$20億、2032年到期的可轉換優先票據，另附加發行$3億的選擇權。資金將用於癌症疫苗業務及償還債務。股價走高有利於設定較高轉換價，也能在轉換發生時減少所需發行的股數，把部分融資選擇交給股權連結型投資人。消息公布後，該股盤前下跌5%，提醒市場：發行人的融資成本下降，仍可能讓既有股東承擔稀釋與供給成本。

相較整體發債總額，這些交易更精確地指出目前AI與創新週期所處位置。強勁終端需求正在動員資本，而非消除資本成本。成熟發行人須支付產業溢價，基礎設施載體必須把長期合約轉化為可融資的擔保品與財務約款，股權連結型借款人則利用波動降低現金票息。對固定收益市場而言，就在Fed辯論金融環境是否具有限制性之際，市場仍在競逐存續期間與資產負債表承接能力。

## 全球緊縮擴大

南韓在本次觀察期間採取最強烈的實際政策行動。韓國央行以6比1決議，將7天期附買回利率上調25個基點至3%，為連續第2次升息，也是逾3年來首度連續升息。總裁Shin Hyun Song將此舉定位為預先行動，以免日後付出更高代價。政策急迫性來自以半導體為主的經濟表現強於預期：韓國央行將2026年成長預測由2.6%上調至3.3%，並預估2027年成長2.9%；同時維持今年2.7%、明年2.3%的通膨預測。其6個月利率指引的21個點位中，有10個集中於3.25%，顯示官員即使正在評估先前2次升息的影響，仍傾向再升息1次。決議公布後，韓元兌美元一度升至1,377.30。

菲律賓儘管成長遠為疲弱，仍連續第3次會議升息。菲律賓中央銀行將目標隔夜反向附買回利率上調25個基點至5%，符合25名經濟學家中20人的預期。通膨約為目標的2倍，央行預期2026年與2027年平均通膨率都將超過4%的容忍上限，至2028年才回到接近3%。進口油價、聖嬰現象與薪資構成上行風險；第2季經濟僅成長2.3%，低於預期，在東南亞主要經濟體中僅優於泰國。這項決策顯示，當輸入性價格傳導足夠劇烈時，匯率與通膨防衛可以凌駕景氣疲弱。

盧安達也明確把抑制通膨置於成長之上，但利率水準更高。盧安達國家銀行將政策利率上調50個基點至8.75%，創2009年以來最高，也是連續第3次升息。城市通膨自4月以來持續呈雙位數，受新鮮食品、肉類與能源成本影響，已升至14.5%。央行預期2026年平均通膨率為13.1%、2027年為7.9%；聖嬰現象與中東緊張局勢使風險分布偏向上行。不同於暫停行動、評估戰事影響的其他央行，盧安達正透過升息限制第二輪效應，以免通膨在回到2%至8%區間前進一步擴散。

澳洲目前的調整反映在預期，而非政策決議。通膨偏熱，加上澳洲儲備銀行對上行意外的容忍度低，使Commonwealth Bank、ANZ與Goldman Sachs轉而預期11月升息，Deutsche Bank與National Australia Bank則預期9月行動。交易員已完全計入11月前升息25個基點，並認為9月升息機率約為五五波。3年期公債殖利率上升7個基點至4.67%，創逾1個月新高。7月家庭支出月增1.1%、年增7%，進一步支持鷹派重估。部分經濟學家仍預期按兵不動，理由是成長疲弱、房價下跌，以及澳洲儲備銀行對月度通膨數據持謹慎態度；因此，定價調整幅度雖大，市場意見仍不一致。

日本的訊號較為細微，因市場已大致計入9月行動。副總裁Ryozo Himino表示，官員應更重視價格上行風險，且未反駁市場對下月升息的預期。隔夜交換仍隱含約82%的機率。然而，日圓兌美元仍一度貶至159.40，因演說並未提出比市場既有預期更強的承諾。若9月升息，將是Kazuo Ueda擔任總裁以來兩次升息間隔最短的一次；但Himino也強調，若延後行動可能迫使日後更大幅調整，日本央行不必等待完美資訊。匯率反應顯示，單次升息已不足以扭轉利差與石油進口負擔；兩項因素使日圓在協同干預將匯價由約164拉升至155.23後，再度逼近160。

歐洲央行7月會議紀要顯示，類似辯論已轉向政策終點，而非眼前一步。部分官員原本會支持升息，並質疑是否存在任何無須再次升息的情境；然而，面對通膨持續性的不確定性，全體委員仍支持維持利率不變。存款利率目前為2.25%，官員討論是否需要維持略具限制性的設定，才能使通膨回到2%；首席經濟學家Philip Lane曾將2.5%形容為中性利率區間上緣。會議紀要顯示，支持進一步緊縮的委員人數增加，但對政策限制過度的疑慮仍未消除。

泰國仍是同步週期的反例。總裁Vitai Ratanakorn否定市場認為1%政策利率將長期維持不變的假設，但表示目前沒有足夠證據支持任何一個方向。若通膨持續或泰銖大幅走弱，升息可能合理；若出現新的經濟衝擊，則可能降息。進一步寬鬆或難以透過銀行有效傳導，且會降低存款人收入與未來政策空間。連續3次按兵不動後，這種有條件的雙向立場是政策指引的重要變化，但不代表升息已成為基準情境。

整體而言，各國行動使全球存續期間對本地通膨持續性的敏感度提高，不再只取決於單一Fed路徑。南韓、菲律賓與盧安達分別因成長、匯率及供給壓力的不同組合實際升息。澳洲因通膨與需求而大幅重定價，日本接受加速政策正常化的高機率，ECB則辯論是否將利率推升至中性水準以上。即使成長疲弱的例外仍然明顯，緊縮範圍擴大仍提高全球債券持續反彈的門檻。

## 損失吸收轉為工具選擇問題

瑞士國會議員正將UBS資本爭論的焦點，從所需資本規模轉向由何種工具承擔損失。政府要求UBS滿足約$200億額外資本需求，並提議以普通股權第一類資本全額支應海外子公司。國會委員會則在評估，重新設計的其他第一類資本債券能否以較低成本承擔更大比重。UBS具有直接市場利益：其流通在外AT1債務約占2,860億歐元歐洲市場的7%；Credit Suisse倒閉以來的不確定性，也不時推高投資人對瑞士工具要求的殖利率。

擬議設計將使AT1在進入處置程序前就開始吸收損失。依據影響委員會討論的學術架構，一旦資本低於監管要求，AT1票息將與股利及管理階層獎金一併暫停。若第一階段未能使銀行恢復穩健，持有人可能獲准自願轉換為股權，同時UBS辦理現金增資。這套程序試圖讓債券發揮持續經營資本的功能，而非等到紓困時才承擔損失；Credit Suisse的$170億減記正是在該時點引發訴訟，並打擊市場對此資產類別的信心。

折衷方案仍具爭議。財政部長Karin Keller-Sutter主張，普通股權是唯一可靠的持續經營損失吸收工具；瑞士國家銀行也持續支持以CET1全額支應海外單位。與國際規範相容同樣不可或缺；若投資人或其他監管機關不接受瑞士特有的AT1，便無法提供有效資本。上議院經濟委員會預定於8月31日處理此案，最終由國會決定。結果將同時影響UBS滿足資本要求的成本，以及歐洲最大銀行資本市場之一的合約架構。

China Vanke面對的損失吸收問題更為迫切。上半年虧損由一年前的人民幣119.5億元擴大至149.5億元，使2024年以來累計虧損達人民幣1,530億元。即使10檔公開發行債券已獲展期，且Shenzhen Metro提供大量支持，營運資金仍然吃緊；後者去年借出逾人民幣300億元，今年上半年再借出45億元。這些貸款支應了債券展期所需的預付款項，卻未恢復營運現金流。Vanke票息3.975%的美元債價格接近55美分，3.5%票據則接近51美分。

下一個合約壓力將在12月中旬到來，屆時一檔票息3%的人民幣債券將於展期後到期，原到期日為去年底。Vanke表示，將針對明年6月前到期的公開發行債券擬定償付計畫，包括可能再次展期。Shenzhen主管機關已安排由國企相關主管主導的董事會，但任何新增股東支持的規模與受償順位仍不明朗。核心信用問題已不再是官方關係能否延後付款，而是新增支持能否填補持續營運虧損，同時避免一再把到期風險轉嫁給既有債權人。

高收益市政融資則在困境發生前就展現選擇性。今年發行人已籌資$33億，較前一年的紀錄速度低約5%，即使整體市政債市場規模約領先6%。休士頓非營利組織QCF/I在銀行將提議殖利率提高至8%後，擱置一筆未評等發行案；另一個未評等專案也未能售出。絕對殖利率升高，加上投資級與較高風險債券之間的補償差距縮小，降低投資人接受薄弱結構的誘因。首次違約共有33件，總額$28.1億，仍接近歷史經驗，因此交易失敗反映承銷紀律，而非市場全面關閉。

這項紀律也解釋了為何在股市強勁上漲的交易日，廣泛信用債工具仍幾乎沒有變動。只要投資人能辨識現金流、擔保品與損失順位，融資管道仍然開放；若承諾的殖利率不足以補償不確定性，資金就會變得昂貴或無法取得。UBS試圖在危機前建立可信的合約觸發條件，Vanke則在虧損發生後仰賴國企相關流動性，市政債買家則在投入資本前拒絕薄弱結構。三者分別處於同一固定收益問題的不同階段：損失由誰承擔，以及這項義務何時可被強制執行？

## 主權信用面對上升的持有成本

哥倫比亞新政府為異常艱難的預算計算提出正式調整路徑。政府計畫在前任政府暫停規則後，於2028年恢復財政規則，並擬提出財政調整法案，將基本赤字占GDP比重降低2.2個百分點。然而，2027年預算仍預估整體赤字占GDP 9.4%。支出將增加16%至635兆披索，約合$2,010億，部分原因是債務服務支出成長逾50%至155兆披索。計畫借款總額約239兆披索，其中約63%於國內籌措，37%向海外籌措。

恢復規則是可信度訊號，但延後2年與短期融資負擔，使其無法發揮立即財政整頓的作用。營運支出393兆披索、投資支出87兆披索，使債務服務成為主要邊際成本。政府主張，此舉是在認列前任政府低估的負債；這雖使9.4%的預估更透明，卻未降低籌資難度。因此，投資人必須依據當前預算評估最終調整法案，而目前利息支出升高本身就會帶來更多借款。

印尼顯示，即使外部信心原本正在改善，本地政治溢價仍可能迅速中斷這項趨勢。數千名示威者因貪腐、生活成本與政府問責問題聚集在國會。午後緊張升高後，議員承諾在12月15日前通過資產沒收法，否則辭職，協助群眾情緒降溫。印尼盾兌美元收盤貶值0.1%至17,726，盤中一度貶值0.4%；10年期公債連續第3日下跌，殖利率當日上升3個基點至7.08%。隨著更廣泛暴力抗議的風險消退，股市收盤上漲1.8%。

印尼資產在交易時段內回穩，具有重要分析意義。這場示威背後的聯盟，規模與團結程度都不及一年前的全國性運動，主要學生及勞工團體均未動員。這支持週四走勢只是暫時政治溢價，而非債務基本面改變的判斷。不過，事件前資金由印尼盾債券轉向美元債券，顯示即使投資人未全面撤離該主權債，本幣存續期間仍對治理風險敏感。

印度的匯率防衛，呈現能源衝擊的另一種成本。印度儲備銀行在盧比走弱時的干預已更為常態化；自6月以來流入的$730億美元資金提供支持，央行上月更在單日投入$70億。油價上升使經常帳逆差擴大，同時印度與美國的利差正在縮小。干預已協助將短期盧比波動率壓至接近10個月低點，但這是在動用資產負債表能力，以緩和源自能源進口與相對利率的壓力。穩定匯率可以減緩傳導，卻無法消除根本的外部成本。

這些主權案例區分了政策承諾與當前融資機制。哥倫比亞承諾未來恢復財政規則，但眼前仍面對龐大赤字與成長逾50%的債務服務支出。印尼議員提出具體期限的政治承諾，平息當下抗議，但本地債券仍承擔較高風險溢價。印度透過反覆干預降低匯率波動，但油價仍使外部收支承受曝險。各國正透過未來財政法規、政治讓步或動用外匯存底來換取可信度，而每一種機制的有效期間與資產負債表極限都不相同。

## 前瞻市場意義

Warsh演說與非農就業年度基準初步修訂值，均將於8月28日紐約時間上午10:00公布。前一次非農就業基準修訂為-91.1萬人，因此即使最新每週初領失業救濟金結果不變，新估值仍可能大幅改變市場對勞動需求強度的衡量。若就業人數大幅下修，且Warsh提出重視通膨廣度與持續性的政策框架，則即使週四鷹派官員發言強硬，7月按兵不動的決定仍可獲得支持。若勞動市場調整較小，或演說將3.7%通膨與穩健的初領失業救濟金數據視為政策限制不足的證據，政策辯論將靠向Hammack與Schmid；2年至5年期債券將承受最直接的重定價，長端反應則取決於政策框架是否清晰。

全球緊縮論點如今取決於目前指引是否轉化為行動，而不是另一則籠統的通膨消息。澳洲第2季GDP與勞動數據將決定，面對通膨偏熱與房市疲弱的衝突，市場對9月升息約五五波的定價能否維持。日本央行總裁Ueda預計在20國集團會議後發言，之後還有Hajime Takata與Kazuyuki Masu發表談話，屆時可觀察官員是否願意縮短升息間隔。若澳洲需求展現韌性，且日本政策正常化路徑更陡，全球存續期間將持續承壓；若經濟活動轉弱或官員明確反駁，則會顯示當地殖利率曲線與匯率已計入多少緊縮預期。

接下來的融資決策將檢驗，投資人取得的報酬是否足以補償正確的法律曝險。Volta的$50億融資最終條款，必須將Anthropic合約與擔保品、攤還安排及發起人支持連結；瑞士委員會8月31日的決定，則必須說明具有提前觸發機制的AT1，能否在UBS資本計畫中可信地取代普通股權。若需求強勁且保障條款未放寬，便可證明市場仍能在具紀律的條件下提供融資。若需要更大規模保證、貸款人保障轉弱，或AT1折衷方案遭到否決，則會強化以下結論：資本充裕並未降低或有槓桿或可靠損失吸收機制的成本。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 27 U.S. fixed-income close extended the Treasury selloff by the smallest possible increment, yet the composition kept the burden of proof on investors expecting policy relief. The 2-year yield rose 1 basis point to 4.20%, the 10-year added 1 basis point to 4.67%, and the 30-year increased 1 basis point to 5.19%. The parallel move left 2s10s unchanged at 47 basis points and 2s30s unchanged at 99 basis points. At 10 years, the real yield held at 2.34% and breakeven inflation rose 1 basis point to 2.33%, locating the day's marginal pressure in inflation compensation rather than another increase in the real discount rate. Treasury supply was not the obstacle: yields remained higher after a $44 billion 7-year auction drew solid demand. The market instead carried a modest premium into Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address as current data and Fed commentary made the reaction function less settled.

The new U.S. evidence leaned in both directions, but the inflation-sensitive side had the stronger ownership of the close. Initial jobless claims fell to 203,000 in the week ended August 22 from a revised 207,000, below the 208,000 consensus, and continuing claims stood at 1.778 million. That is not a labor-market break that would force the Fed to look through above-target inflation. The advanced July goods-trade deficit widened sharply to $118.8 billion from $101.4 billion, against a $99 billion consensus. The larger deficit complicates the growth reading, but it also points to a heavier external financing need rather than an automatic disinflation signal. Against that mix, Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both argued that the current setting is not restraining the economy enough, whereas Boston Fed President Susan Collins continued to call it mildly restrictive and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee wanted more evidence on services inflation. The close priced a live debate over whether restraint exists at all, not merely how long it should be maintained.

Risk appetite placed an important limit on the bearish rates interpretation. Nvidia's outlook drove the Nasdaq 100 up 1.43% and the semiconductor index up 2.33%; the S&P 500 gained 0.72% even though most of its constituents declined, and the VIX fell 4.60% to 14.51. Broad credit total-return funds were nearly unchanged rather than signaling a disorderly withdrawal of financing. WTI rose 1.57% to $83.52 and Brent gained 0.82% to $88.56 as diplomacy around the Strait of Hormuz encountered fresh obstacles, reversing part of the previous session's energy relief. Physical flows through the strait have nevertheless recovered to roughly 6 million to 8 million barrels a day, still only about half their prewar level. The simultaneous strength in technology equities, oil and breakevens is more consistent with resilient nominal demand and unresolved supply pressure than with a generalized fiscal panic.

The investment-committee judgment is therefore narrow but consequential. Treasury yields moved only 1 basis point, yet neither firm labor claims, a wider trade gap, a revived oil price nor a more vocal hawkish Fed contingent allowed the prior session's conditional hold to become comfortable. Strong AI demand added a separate challenge: it supported equity growth expectations while intensifying competition for labor, equipment, power and bond-market capacity. Global central banks reinforced that pressure through actual rate increases and firmer guidance. Confidence in a sustained U.S. selloff remains limited because the curve did not steepen, 10-year real yields did not rise, the 7-year auction cleared with solid demand, and physical oil exports continued to recover. Warsh now has to decide whether to validate the market's modest inflation premium with a clearer tightening framework or contain long-rate volatility by explaining how the Fed will distinguish concentrated AI strength and supply shocks from economy-wide overheating.

## The Fed Debate Shifts to Whether Policy Restrains

Schmid supplied the day's clearest incremental policy signal. The Kansas City Fed president said the current rate setting might be accommodative at the short end and placed himself near the officials who favored a July hike. With the federal funds target at 3.5% to 3.75% and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge up 3.7% over the year through July, his argument is that policymakers still have work to do before policy can be described as restrictive. That is a stronger claim than preserving the option of another increase. It questions the starting point from which the committee is assessing inflation persistence.

Hammack independently broadened that view and attached a timing preference. The Cleveland Fed president, one of three officials who dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase in July, said officials should act now because rates are not cooling the economy sufficiently. She expects inflation to finish 2026 around 3% and sees only limited progress toward the mid-2% area next year. Her concern is not that inflation expectations have already broken; she said they have not. It is that more than five years above target could eventually change household behavior. Hammack also pointed to exceptionally active equity and debt capital markets as evidence that financing conditions are not delivering enough restraint. The argument links the reaction function to observed risk-taking and issuance, not only to lagging inflation data.

Collins described a more conventional transmission mechanism. The Boston Fed president, who does not vote this year and supported the July hold, still sees mild restriction in housing and among smaller businesses. Her continued support for holding depends on evidence that inflation is easing, particularly if tariffs, Middle East developments or other supply shocks add persistence. She also judged inflation expectations compatible with the 2% objective. That qualification prevents the hawkish case from becoming a consensus: parts of the economy are responding to high borrowing costs, and credibility measures have not forced immediate action.

Goolsbee's threshold sharpened the source of the disagreement. The Chicago Fed president is prepared to wait for evidence on whether the current inflation shock persists, with services prices the critical area. Continued high or worsening services inflation would make him more concerned; cooling would preserve room for patience. The committee is consequently divided across three questions that should not be collapsed into a single hawkish-dovish spectrum: whether current policy is restrictive, whether supply-driven inflation will spread, and how much evidence is needed before acting. Schmid and Hammack answer the first question negatively. Collins sees restraint already operating. Goolsbee puts the next decision on the breadth and persistence of services inflation.

Thursday's releases did not resolve those disagreements. Claims at 203,000 were 5,000 below consensus and 4,000 below the revised prior reading, supporting the view that the labor market remains firm enough to tolerate tighter policy. The $17.4 billion widening in the goods deficit was much larger than anticipated, but it cannot by itself identify the domestic-demand or inventory contribution. Its immediate fixed-income relevance lies in the combination of uncertain growth accounting and a larger external imbalance. Neither release supplied the broad demand deterioration that would make a 4.20% 2-year yield obviously too high.

Short-rate trading still resisted an imminent increase. A block purchase of 45,000 October federal funds futures contracts was consistent with no move before December even as the broader market assigned roughly a one-third probability to September and priced a quarter-point increase by year-end. That disagreement between outspoken officials and event-date pricing explains why the coupon curve moved in parallel instead of repricing the front end aggressively. Investors paid a modest premium for Warsh risk without treating Schmid and Hammack as a settled committee majority.

The long end carried a related communications premium. A clear inflation reaction function could reduce uncertainty around the path even if its level is hawkish; silence would leave every supply shock, data release and Treasury operation to set the marginal policy narrative. The unchanged 2s30s slope shows that Thursday did not become a fresh debt-sustainability steepener. Still, a 5.19% 30-year yield alongside a 4.20% 2-year yield leaves almost a full percentage point between the two, so ambiguity over how monetary and debt-management policy interact remains expensive. Warsh's task is not simply to sound restrictive. It is to explain which evidence can move the Fed and which balance-sheet questions remain outside the rate decision.

## AI Growth Raises Both Demand and Funding Costs

Nvidia converted the AI demand story from projected capital spending into a realized corporate growth signal. The company forecast roughly 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, compared with the 45% pace analysts had expected, and projected current-period revenue of $108 billion, up 89% from a year earlier. Its shares rose nearly 9%, adding about $442 billion of market value, and pulled technology benchmarks higher. Smaller customers generated about $40 billion, or 42%, of quarterly revenue, more than twice their share a year earlier. That breadth reduces the argument that demand rests only on a handful of hyperscalers, even as supply constraints in memory, wafers and packaging remain central to delivery.

For fixed income, the same outlook strengthens the nominal-demand channel that Schmid highlighted. Data-center construction competes for labor, machinery, materials and electricity. Goods-producing and construction wage growth has accelerated relative to services even with weak housing construction, and Schmid said AI investment is intensifying competition in his district. The macro question is whether those pressures remain concentrated enough for the Fed to tolerate or spread broadly enough to sustain services and wage inflation. Thursday's 1-basis-point rise in 10-year breakevens, alongside an unchanged real yield, is directionally compatible with a small reassessment of that inflation channel. A single basis point cannot establish the cause, but the price composition fits better with nominal resilience than with a growth scare.

Nvidia's disclosed commitments reveal how equity optimism can create creditor exposure before conventional debt appears. The company has committed $279 billion of future spending, much of it with Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Micron Technology and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. It has also promised as much as $56 billion for data-center usage even if capacity is not taken up and assumed $109 billion of loan guarantees, mostly connected with a large Ohio data center for OpenAI. Purchase commitments, usage guarantees and credit guarantees occupy different legal positions, yet all can compete for cash when utilization, customer quality or refinancing conditions disappoint. The realized sales outlook improves the revenue side of that equation; it does not make the contingent obligations disappear.

Bond investors are already charging the sector for absorption. Hyperscalers have raised more than $220 billion this year in seven currencies, and Matthias Reschke, JPMorgan's head of European investment-grade finance, put their U.S. spread premium at about 55 basis points over other corporate debt. His conclusion was that placement remains available at a price. The premium is therefore not a closed-market signal. It is the clearing cost of concentrating unusually large issuance among borrowers that can quickly become dominant nonfinancial names in smaller currencies.

Volta Infrastructure puts a defined transaction around the next layer of the buildout. JPMorgan has begun sounding lenders for a $5 billion debt package to finance the new company's data centers. Volta had secured $300 million of venture funding at a $2.4 billion valuation and signed a six-year, $10 billion agreement to provide Anthropic with computing capacity at a Norwegian site managed with Bitdeer Technologies. The financing depends on a contractual customer relationship, site delivery and infrastructure execution rather than the unsecured credit of a mature hyperscaler. Final leverage, collateral, amortization, guarantees and lender protections will determine whether the contract is enough to support the requested debt.

Other borrowers are adapting their funding venue to the same competition for capital. Fortescue is considering its first panda bond, a roughly 3 billion yuan issue through Fortescue Treasury (China) guaranteed by the parent, with investor meetings planned for early September and possible marketing in October. The company has applied to issue as much as 20 billion yuan over two years. Panda issuance has carried an average 1.88% coupon this year, more than 200 basis points below the 3-year U.S. Treasury yield, giving Fortescue a low-cost diversification route even as a dispute with China's state-backed iron-ore buyer disrupts some exports. Funding access and commercial tension sit in the same structure: the parent guarantee supports local investors, while the issuer's China relationship creates part of the reason to diversify markets and sales.

Moderna used a different asset-price window. After positive cancer-vaccine trial results drove a 177% one-day share gain on August 19, the company announced $2 billion of convertible senior notes due 2032, with an option for another $300 million. Proceeds will fund the cancer-vaccine business and repay debt. The higher share price supports a higher conversion price and reduces the number of shares needed if conversion occurs, transferring part of the financing choice to equity-linked investors. Its stock fell 5% before the open after the announcement, a reminder that cheaper financing for the issuer can still impose dilution and supply costs on existing holders.

These transactions locate the present AI and innovation cycle more precisely than aggregate issuance totals. Strong end demand is mobilizing capital, not eliminating its price. Mature issuers pay a sector premium, infrastructure vehicles must translate long contracts into bankable collateral and covenants, and equity-linked borrowers exploit volatility to reduce cash coupons. The fixed-income consequence is continued competition for duration and balance sheet at the same time the Fed is debating whether those financial conditions are restrictive.

## Global Tightening Gains Breadth

South Korea delivered the strongest realized policy action in the window. The Bank of Korea raised its 7-day repurchase rate 25 basis points to 3% in a 6-1 decision, its second consecutive increase and the first back-to-back tightening sequence in more than three years. Governor Shin Hyun Song framed the move as preemptive action against a later, more costly response. The urgency came from a semiconductor-led economy that is running stronger than expected: the BOK lifted its 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% from 2.6% and projected 2.9% growth in 2027, while keeping inflation forecasts at 2.7% this year and 2.3% next year. Ten of 21 points in its six-month guidance clustered at 3.25%, suggesting one additional increase even as officials assess the two already delivered. The won strengthened as far as 1,377.30 per dollar after the decision.

The Philippines tightened for a third consecutive meeting despite much weaker growth. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas raised its target reverse-repurchase rate 25 basis points to 5%, matching the expectation of 20 of 25 economists. Inflation is running about twice the target, and the bank expects its average rate to exceed the 4% tolerance ceiling in both 2026 and 2027 before returning near 3% in 2028. Imported oil, El Nino and wages create upside risk, while Q2 growth of 2.3% was slower than expected and stronger only than Thailand among the major Southeast Asian economies. The decision shows that currency and inflation defense can dominate cyclical weakness when the imported-price channel is sufficiently acute.

Rwanda made the same priority explicit at a higher level. The National Bank of Rwanda lifted its policy rate 50 basis points to 8.75%, the highest since 2009 and its third successive increase. Urban inflation has held in double digits since April and reached 14.5% on fresh food, meat and energy costs. The bank expects inflation to average 13.1% in 2026 and 7.9% in 2027, with El Nino and Middle East tensions keeping the distribution skewed upward. Unlike peers that have paused to assess the war's effects, Rwanda is using rates to limit second-round effects before inflation returns to its 2% to 8% range.

Australia's current adjustment occurred through expectations rather than a policy decision. Hot inflation and the Reserve Bank of Australia's low tolerance for an upside surprise pushed Commonwealth Bank, ANZ and Goldman Sachs toward a November increase, with Deutsche Bank and National Australia Bank calling for September. Traders fully priced a 25-basis-point move by November and assigned roughly even odds to September. The 3-year government yield rose 7 basis points to 4.67%, its highest in more than a month. July household spending reinforced the hawkish revision by rising 1.1% on the month and 7% from a year earlier. Some economists still expect a hold, citing weak growth, falling housing prices and the RBA's caution about monthly inflation data, so the repricing is forceful but not unanimous.

Japan's signal was subtler because much of the September move was already discounted. Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino said officials should pay greater attention to upside price risks and did not push back against expectations for a rate increase next month. Overnight swaps continued to imply about an 82% probability. The yen nevertheless weakened briefly to 159.40 per dollar because the speech offered no stronger commitment than the market already carried. A September increase would create the shortest interval between hikes under Governor Kazuo Ueda, but Himino also emphasized that the Bank of Japan need not wait for perfect information when delayed action could require a sharper later move. The currency response shows that one hike alone is no longer enough to reverse a rate differential and oil-import burden that have pulled the yen back toward 160 after coordinated intervention lifted it from roughly 164 to 155.23.

The European Central Bank's July account revealed a similar debate over the destination rather than the immediate step. Some officials would have supported an increase and questioned whether any scenario could avoid another hike, yet all members backed the decision to hold amid uncertainty over inflation persistence. With the deposit rate at 2.25%, officials discussed whether a mildly restrictive setting may be needed to return inflation to 2%; Chief Economist Philip Lane has described 2.5% as the upper end of neutral. The minutes add committee breadth to the case for further tightening without removing concern about excessive restraint.

Thailand remains the counterexample to a synchronized cycle. Governor Vitai Ratanakorn rejected the market's assumption that the 1% policy rate will remain unchanged for an extended period, but he said there is currently insufficient evidence for either direction. Persistent inflation or sharp baht weakness could justify a hike; a new economic shock could justify a cut. Further easing may transmit poorly through banks and would reduce depositor income and future policy space. That conditional two-way stance is a material change in guidance after three holds, not evidence that a hike has become the base case.

Together, these actions make global duration more sensitive to local inflation persistence than to a single Fed path. Korea, the Philippines and Rwanda delivered actual increases for different combinations of growth, currency and supply pressure. Australia repriced sharply on inflation and demand, Japan accepted high odds of faster normalization, and the ECB debated moving beyond neutral. The breadth raises the hurdle for a durable global bond rally even though weak-growth exceptions remain visible.

## Loss Absorption Becomes an Instrument Question

Swiss lawmakers are moving the UBS capital debate from the size of the requirement to the instrument that bears losses. The government wants UBS to meet roughly $20 billion of additional capital needs and has proposed backing foreign subsidiaries fully with common equity Tier 1. A parliamentary committee is considering whether redesigned Additional Tier 1 bonds could cover a larger share at lower cost. UBS has a direct market interest: its outstanding AT1 debt represents about 7% of the EUR286 billion European market, and uncertainty since Credit Suisse's collapse has periodically raised the yield demanded on Swiss instruments.

The proposed redesign would make AT1 loss absorption begin before resolution. Under the academic framework influencing the committee, falling below regulatory capital requirements would suspend AT1 coupons together with dividends and management bonuses. If that first stage failed to restore the bank, holders could be offered voluntary conversion into equity while UBS conducted a rights issue. This sequence attempts to make the bonds function as going-concern capital instead of waiting until the point of rescue, when Credit Suisse's $17 billion write-off generated litigation and damaged confidence in the asset class.

The compromise remains contested. Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter argues that common equity is the only reliable going-concern loss absorber, and the Swiss National Bank continues to support full CET1 backing for foreign units. International compatibility is also essential; a uniquely Swiss AT1 that investors or other regulators reject would not provide useful capital. The upper-house economic committee is due to address the issue on August 31, and parliament will ultimately decide. The outcome will affect both UBS's cost of meeting the requirement and the contractual architecture of one of Europe's largest bank-capital markets.

China Vanke presents a more immediate loss-absorption problem. Its first-half loss widened to 14.95 billion yuan from 11.95 billion yuan a year earlier, taking cumulative losses since 2024 to 153 billion yuan. Working capital remains tight despite extensions of 10 public bonds and extensive support from Shenzhen Metro, which lent more than 30 billion yuan last year and another 4.5 billion yuan in the first half. Those loans enabled upfront payments for bond extensions, but they have not restored operating cash generation. Vanke's 3.975% dollar bond traded near 55 cents and its 3.5% note near 51 cents.

The next contractual pressure arrives in mid-December, when an extended 3% yuan bond matures after originally coming due late last year. Vanke said it will formulate repayment plans, including possible extensions, for public bonds maturing through next June. Shenzhen authorities have installed a board dominated by state-linked executives, but the scale and seniority of any additional shareholder support remain unclear. The core credit issue is no longer whether official ties can postpone payment. It is whether new support can bridge persistent operating losses without repeatedly transferring maturity risk to existing creditors.

High-yield municipal finance showed selectivity before distress rather than after it. Issuers have raised $3.3 billion this year, about 5% below the prior year's record pace, even as the broader municipal market is roughly 6% ahead. The Houston nonprofit QCF/I shelved an unrated offering after bankers raised the proposed yield to 8%, and another unrated project failed to sell. Higher absolute yields and tighter compensation between investment-grade and riskier bonds have reduced the incentive to accept weak structures. Thirty-three first-time defaults totaling $2.81 billion remain close to historical experience, so the failed deals point to underwriting discipline rather than a generalized market closure.

That discipline also explains why broad credit vehicles barely moved during a strong equity session. Financing remains open where investors can identify cash flow, collateral and loss position. It becomes expensive or unavailable when the promised yield does not compensate for uncertainty. UBS is trying to make contractual triggers credible before a crisis, Vanke is relying on state-linked liquidity after losses have materialized, and municipal buyers are rejecting structures before capital is committed. Each is a different stage of the same fixed-income question: who absorbs loss, and when does that obligation become enforceable?

## Sovereign Credibility Meets Rising Carry Costs

Colombia's new administration attached a formal adjustment path to an unusually difficult budget arithmetic. It plans to restore the fiscal rule in 2028 after the previous government suspended it, and it intends to propose a fiscal-adjustment bill that would reduce the primary deficit by 2.2 percentage points of GDP. The 2027 budget nevertheless projects an overall deficit of 9.4% of GDP. Spending would rise 16% to 635 trillion pesos, or about $201 billion, driven partly by debt service that jumps more than 50% to 155 trillion pesos. Planned borrowing totals roughly 239 trillion pesos, with about 63% raised domestically and 37% overseas.

Restoring the rule is a credibility signal, but the two-year delay and near-term financing burden prevent it from functioning as immediate consolidation. Operating spending of 393 trillion pesos and investment of 87 trillion pesos leave debt service as a dominant marginal cost. The government argues that it is recognizing liabilities understated by its predecessor, which makes the 9.4% projection more transparent but does not make it easier to fund. Investors must therefore assess the eventual adjustment legislation against a current budget in which higher interest expense itself drives more borrowing.

Indonesia showed how quickly a local political premium can interrupt otherwise improving external confidence. Thousands of demonstrators gathered at parliament over corruption, living costs and government accountability. Legislators promised to pass an asset-forfeiture law by December 15 or resign, helping calm the crowd after tensions rose during the afternoon. The rupiah finished 0.1% weaker at 17,726 per dollar after losing as much as 0.4%, and the 10-year government yield rose 3 basis points to 7.08% for a third day of losses. Equities closed 1.8% higher as the risk of a broader violent protest receded.

The recovery in Indonesian assets within the session is analytically important. The coalition behind the demonstration was smaller and less unified than the nationwide movement a year earlier, with major student and labor groups not mobilizing. That supports the view that Thursday's move was a temporary political premium rather than a change in debt fundamentals. Rotation from rupiah bonds into dollar bonds before the event nevertheless shows that local-currency duration remains sensitive to governance risk even when investors do not abandon the sovereign altogether.

India's currency defense illustrates a different cost of the energy shock. The Reserve Bank of India has become more routine in its intervention when the rupee weakens, supported by $73 billion of dollar inflows since June, and spent $7 billion in a single day last month. Higher oil prices widen the current-account deficit as the interest-rate gap with the United States narrows. The intervention has helped push near-term rupee volatility close to a 10-month low, but it uses balance-sheet capacity to smooth a pressure that originates in energy imports and relative rates. Stability can slow pass-through without eliminating the underlying external cost.

These sovereign cases separate promises from current financing mechanics. Colombia has committed to a future rule while confronting a large present deficit and a more than 50% increase in debt service. Indonesian lawmakers supplied a dated political commitment that calmed an immediate protest, but local bonds still carried a higher risk premium. India has reduced currency volatility through repeated intervention while oil keeps the external balance exposed. Credibility is being purchased through future fiscal law, political concession or reserve deployment; each mechanism has a different duration and balance-sheet limit.

## Forward Market Significance

Warsh's address and the preliminary annual payroll revision both arrive at 10:00 a.m. New York time on August 28. The prior payroll benchmark revision was -911,000, so the new estimate can materially alter the measured strength of labor demand even without changing the latest weekly claims result. A large downward revision paired with a Warsh framework that emphasizes breadth and persistence could preserve the July hold despite Thursday's hawkish speakers. A smaller labor adjustment or an address that treats 3.7% inflation and firm claims as evidence of insufficient restraint would pull the policy debate toward Hammack and Schmid, with the 2- to 5-year sector carrying the most direct repricing and the long end responding to the clarity of the framework.

The global tightening thesis now depends on whether current guidance becomes action rather than on another generic inflation headline. Australia's Q2 GDP and labor data will determine whether the market's roughly even September-hike odds survive the conflict between hot prices and weak housing. BOJ Governor Ueda's expected remarks after the Group of 20 gathering, followed by speeches from Hajime Takata and Kazuyuki Masu, will show whether officials are comfortable compressing the interval between hikes. Evidence of resilient demand in Australia and a steeper normalization path in Japan would keep global duration under pressure; weaker activity or explicit pushback would expose how much tightening is already embedded in local curves and currencies.

The next financing decisions will test whether investors are being paid for the correct legal exposure. Final terms on Volta's $5 billion package must connect the Anthropic contract to collateral, amortization and sponsor support, while the Swiss committee's August 31 decision must show whether an early-trigger AT1 can credibly substitute for common equity in UBS's capital plan. Strong demand without looser protections would demonstrate that capacity remains available at disciplined terms. A need for larger guarantees, weaker lender safeguards or a rejection of the AT1 compromise would reinforce the conclusion that abundant capital has not reduced the price of contingent leverage or reliable loss absorption.

Indonesia's temporary political premium and India's reserve-backed currency smoothing show that confidence can be stabilized, but only through finite policy capacity.
